findings.reason: I checked this: when the federated update succeeds, the new branch never deletes the local recovery-codes credential, and UserCredentialManager.isValid passes any input the federated validator rejects on to the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider, so stale local codes still work in the upgrade scenario described; real, but it needs that specific migration state.

I checked this: the authenticator now picks up the federated credential but calls removeStoredCredentialById, which goes only to the local store, and nothing tells user storage that a code was used; the test provider never consumes codes, so codes can be reused and the page always asks for code #1. It is a real design gap, but consuming codes is arguably the federated provider's job.

Confirmed: the new getCredentials override returns the OTP model, and the PR also gives OTP an id, so testOTPSetupThroughAdminRESTAndLogin now goes through the getFederatedCredentialsStream path in CredentialDeleteHelper:64 instead of the legacy 'otp-id' placeholder path, which no longer has a test; this is a test-coverage concern.

Correct: createFromValues never sets an id and the generated recoveryCodes id is thrown away, so the federated credential shows up with a null id and cannot be deleted; but this only affects the test provider and does not break any tested path.

Correct: the test logs in once with code 0 and never checks reuse or the next code, so it misses the non-consumption on the federated path, and the alias typo is real; this is a test gap on test-provider behaviour.

The literal does duplicate the factory constant, but that constant is in the services module, which server-spi-private cannot see, so the main fix is not possible; what remains is a minor cleanup (look the provider up lazily).
